skill.name: auth-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze authentication and authorization designs for common security weaknesses and remediation steps.
skill.summary: Review auth code, flows, and reports for password, session, token, and access control risks.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: The static findings are triggered by Markdown examples inside a defensive authentication security guide, not by executable skill code. The weak crypto, curl, fetch, process.env, and token snippets are presented as teaching examples or remediation examples, so no malicious execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Static scanners flag many fenced code examples as executable behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples consistently as illustrative and avoid including runnable attack loops unless needed for defensive explanation.

remediation.issue: The report examples include offensive-looking brute force and bypass demonstrations.
remediation.suggestion: Keep exploit examples scoped to defensive education and pair each with authorization context and mitigation steps.

content.value_statement: Authentication and authorization bugs can expose accounts, sessions, and private data. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused auth reviews with clear remediation advice.
actual_capabilities: Reviews password hashing choices and flags weak storage patterns.
Checks session configuration for fixation, cookie, and timeout risks.
Analyzes JWT and OAuth flows for token validation mistakes.
Evaluates RBAC, ABAC, ownership checks, and privilege escalation paths.
Formats findings with severity, impact, and remediation guidance.
Maps common issues to OWASP and authentication compliance themes.
limitations: Does not run dynamic penetration tests or exploit live systems.
Requires access to relevant auth code, routes, and configuration details.
Cannot prove production controls without logs, deployment settings, or runtime evidence.
May need human validation for business-specific authorization rules.

use_cases.title: Review a login implementation
use_cases.description: Check password hashing, rate limits, session regeneration, and account enumeration defenses before release.

use_cases.title: Audit access control rules
use_cases.description: Find missing ownership checks, overbroad roles, and authorization gaps across protected routes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a remediation report
use_cases.description: Turn auth findings into prioritized fixes with clear impact, severity, and compliance context.

prompt_templates.title: Basic auth check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one authentication file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-analyzer to review this authentication file. Focus on password handling, session setup, and obvious login risks.

prompt_templates.title: JWT and OAuth review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-analyzer to review our JWT and OAuth flow. Check token signing, verification, expiration, issuer, audience, state, and PKCE handling.

prompt_templates.title: Authorization route audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-analyzer to audit these protected routes. Identify missing ownership checks, role bypasses, IDOR risks, and privilege escalation paths.

prompt_templates.title: Full remediation report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use auth-analyzer to produce a prioritized authentication and authorization security report. Include severity, affected flow, exploit impact, and concrete remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a login route that stores MD5 password hashes and returns different errors for unknown users.
output: Critical finding: weak password hashing exposes users if the database is leaked.
Medium finding: different login errors can reveal whether an account exists.
Recommended fix: migrate to Argon2id, use uniform error messages, and add rate limiting.

output_examples.input: Check an API route where authenticated users can update any user ID in the URL.
output: High finding: missing ownership check allows horizontal privilege escalation.
Impact: one user can change another user profile or role if the handler accepts role fields.
Recommended fix: require self-access or admin role, and block role changes for normal users.

output_examples.input: Assess a JWT middleware that decodes token payloads without signature verification.
output: Critical finding: unsigned token payloads can be forged by attackers.
Impact: attackers can impersonate users or admins.
Recommended fix: verify signatures with allowed algorithms, issuer, audience, and short expiration.

best_practices: Provide the full authentication flow, including middleware, routes, models, and configuration.
Ask for prioritized findings with impact and concrete remediation steps.
Validate authorization findings against real business ownership and role rules.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to test live systems without explicit authorization.
Do not review only frontend role checks when backend authorization determines security.
Do not treat example code as production evidence without confirming where it runs.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews authentication and authorization patterns, including passwords, sessions, JWT, OAuth, RBAC, ABAC, and ownership checks.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It helps with code and design review, but it does not perform live exploitation or runtime validation.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide auth middleware, route handlers, token code, session settings, user models, and relevant business access rules.

faq.question: Will it find business logic issues?
faq.answer: It can identify likely authorization gaps, but product-specific rules need review by someone who understands the application.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive code?
faq.answer: Use your normal code handling rules. Remove real secrets before sharing snippets or reports.
